glossary.definition: The role responsible for decisions and records in the defined workflow.
A point where a record moves from one person or system to another.
Statements the team can test when judging software.
Requirements and internal procedures used as a reference for an audit.
What the auditor saw, read or was told, recorded with enough detail for someone else to check it.
A judgment drawn from observations and measured against criteria.

example.label: Illustrative example
example.description: An unnamed Canadian manufacturer evaluates internal audit management software for one production workflow; all situations and records are hypothetical, not customer results.

reviewedChapters.title: Mapping the current workflow: Internal audit management software
reviewedChapters.summary: The page covers the assigned workflow decisions, uses supported citations and clearly labels its hypothetical examples. No FAQ subsection was assigned or included.
decisions: Which workflow break to solve first and whether to accept the problem statement
How to handle missing or disputed records
Which records are authoritative, copies or working notes
How to resolve records without clear owners or in personal storage
Which roles own handoffs and decisions, including backups
How to handle unfilled roles, conflicts of interest and unreachable owners
Who confirms auditor competence and objectivity and reviews results
Which acceptance criteria are must-haves, should-haves or could-haves and what counts as a pass
How to resolve untestable or conflicting criteria

reviewedChapters.title: Evaluating software capabilities: Internal audit management software
reviewedChapters.summary: The page covers the assigned evaluation steps with supported citations, actionable workflow decisions and labeled hypothetical examples. It does not include an unassigned FAQ.
decisions: Which candidates proceed to demonstration or are removed from the shortlist
Whether to request a trial or drop a promising candidate with an undemonstrated must-have
Whether each test scenario passed, failed or was not shown
How to handle a scenario that cannot be run live
Whether evidence and permissions meet the team's criteria and separation rules
Whether to reject a product, change a rule or accept a procedural control when a permission rule cannot be enforced
How to handle an incomplete quote
Which product to recommend and whether the recommendation is provisional
Whether top management approves the final choice

reviewedChapters.title: Planning the internal audit program: Internal audit management software
reviewedChapters.summary: The earlier findings are resolved: each planning step records acceptance or rejection and its decision-maker, and the assignment and scheduling steps identify who revises returned work. No unassigned FAQ is present.
decisions: Define and accept or return program and audit scopes.
Resolve disputed or unclear scope and escalate unresolved issues.
Assign auditors based on competence and impartiality, or return unsuitable assignments.
Choose an added control, delay or outside help when no impartial auditor is available.
Accept or return the calendar based on priorities, representative coverage and reduced-frequency justifications.
Change dates or sampling when an area is unavailable.
Accept or reject requests to move, add or cancel audits.
Decide on short-notice or outside-quality change requests.

reviewedChapters.title: Collecting and connecting audit evidence: Internal audit management software
reviewedChapters.summary: The page covers the assigned evidence workflows with supported citations, actionable decisions and labeled hypothetical examples. It does not include an unassigned FAQ.
decisions: Whether to accept or return the checklist
Whether to write or revise a question when library items are unsuitable or a question is disputed
Whether the observation-recording method is acceptable
Whether to use paper capture when a connection or device is unavailable, and who enters it and when
Whether to accept or return each evidence-to-criterion link
Whether to add a criterion, collect more evidence or note a gap
Which user types may see or change each record type
Whether to accept or return the access configuration
Whether to grant, narrow or refuse temporary access
How to apply the previously taken evaluation decision when a product cannot enforce an access rule

reviewedChapters.title: Recording and reviewing findings: Internal audit management software
reviewedChapters.summary: The page covers all four assigned workflows with supported citations, actionable evaluation questions and labeled hypothetical examples. No FAQ was assigned or included.
decisions: Whether an observation becomes a finding and which category applies.
Whether to request more evidence or escalate an observation that does not fit a category.
Whether evidence is relevant, sufficient and retrievable, or the finding should be returned.
Whether to collect more evidence, hold or withdraw a finding when evidence is inaccessible or disputed.
Who owns the response and by when, and whether to reassign or escalate ownership.
Whether a disputed finding stands, is revised, is withdrawn or is held for more evidence.
Whether a dispute decision has a recorded basis or should be returned for more detail.
Who reviews and accepts a dispute decision when the quality manager is involved.
